correctness.rationale: Stationary two-sided construction gives finite polynomial moments. Exact generator identities yield E[X²]=2Dbar/r, E[X² cos(2θ)]=δ/(r+ω), E[XY sin(2θ)]=δ/(r+ω), and V=4Dbar²/r²+4δ²/[r(r+ω)]>0. Conditional future Y² semigroup closes and forces C′+rC=−[2δ²/(r+ω)]e^{−ωt}; C=e^{−rt}(V−A∫exp((r−ω)s)ds). The normalized bracket is strictly decreasing, and its sign threshold is the positive root of (2+3b²)(r/ω)²−2b²(r/ω)−2=0. Resonance r=ω, equality at r=rc, b→0/isotropic b=0 and b→1 boundaries, and high-rate asymptotics are proved with separate limits. 1477 standard-library checker assertions and 180000-sample path Monte Carlo are supporting finite diagnostics, not proof.

value.rationale: The positive simultaneous cross-energy covariance and isotropic stationary law conceal a rigorously negative delayed cross-energy regime. The natural two-time statistic has a complete global classification: sharp shape-dependent rate r_c, unique lag zero above it, positive critical tail, explicit lag and high-rate asymptotics. This can discriminate a retained rotating anisotropic mobility from a scalar diffusivity bath or synchronous full reset without claiming a downstream paper-sized result. Not a cheap renaming of a one-time kurtosis calculation.
